caption_used: Mean absolute values of hidden states across model layers, comparing pre-gating, post-gating, and baseline configurations. The hidden state mean before gate (blue dashed line, avg 0.71) remains near zero through approximately layer 15, then rises sharply to a peak of roughly 2.8 at layer 23. The post-gating hidden state mean (orange dotted, avg 0.05) and baseline mean (green solid, avg 0.04) both remain close to zero throughout, with the baseline showing marginally higher values than the post-gating mean in the final layers. The dramatic pre-gating increase beginning at layer 12 demonstrates that gating effectively suppresses the activation amplification observed in deeper layers.

raw_responses.Bulgarian:
The figure is a line chart titled "Hidden State Mean" that plots the absolute mean of hidden states across layers for three different configurations: "hidden state mean before gate", "hidden state mean after gate", and "hidden state mean of baseline". The x-axis, labeled "Layer", ranges from 0 to 23 (though the last tick is at 20, the line extends to 23) with integer intervals. The y-axis, labeled "Abs Mean", ranges from 0 to 4 with integer intervals. The "hidden state mean before gate" is represented by a blue dashed line with a stated average of 0.71. This line starts near 0, remains low until approximately layer 15, then rises sharply to a peak of approximately 2.8 at layer 23. The "hidden state mean after gate" is shown as an orange dotted line with an average of 0.05. This line remains very close to zero throughout the entire range. The "hidden state mean of baseline" is depicted as a green solid line with an average of 0.04. This line also remains very close to zero, slightly above the orange line in the final layers.
